title: Every general view, with invented data
summary: A fictional specification that uses each general block once, so a reader can see what each view does before composing one. None of these numbers describes anything real.

story.background: Three invented note-taking tools, **Option A**, **Option B** and **Option C**, are compared on made-up evidence so that every general view of the library appears once with numbers a reader can follow. Option A is the tool in use, B and C the two candidates. None of the numbers describes anything real.
story.intent: Show an author what each general view looks like and how it reads, before they compose a report of their own.
questions: How does each general view present evidence, missing values and uncertainty?
How do the three invented options compare on pass rate, features and head-to-head preference?
story.rule: No real decision rests on this page; if it did, the option with the highest pass rate whose interval clears Option A's would be chosen.
story.covers: Every general block once: text, callouts, lists, facts, a table, a requirement matrix, intervals, bars, a trend, excerpts and a diagram, each with invented values.
story.notCovered: Trial and comparison views, which read real trial or comparison data, and any real tool or measurement.

alternatives.a: The note-taking tool in use today: the reference the other two are held against.
alternatives.b: The first candidate, which shares notes directly within one team.
alternatives.c: The second candidate, which works offline only from a prepared bundle and had few valid runs.

blocks.title: Plain text
text: Paragraphs separate on blank lines. Inline `code` and **emphasis** are the only markup; every other character is shown exactly as supplied, so <tags> in evidence stay text.

blocks.title: What this does not show
blocks.text: A callout states a condition or limit beside the evidence it qualifies.

blocks.title: Open questions
items: Does the effect hold at higher effort?

items.text: Is the judge consistent across orders?

blocks.title: A table with a missing value

read.says: Option B passed 20 runs against 14 for Option A; Option C's word count was not recorded, so the table says missing rather than zero.
Only Option A works fully offline, Option B shares directly, and Option C's offline support needs a prepared bundle.

sections.reading: Option B passed 20 runs against 14 for Option A; Option C's word count was not recorded, so the table says missing rather than zero. In the matrix only Option A works fully offline, Option B shares directly, and Option C's offline support needs a prepared bundle.

sections.title: Quantities
sections.label: Quantities

read.says: Option B's band sits above the half line and clear of Option A's; Option C's band is wide because only four runs back it.
Head to head, Option B was preferred in 12 of 19 pairings with Option A; Option C's losses were not recorded.
Option B's pass rate rose round by round while Option A's stayed near half.

sections.reading: Option B passed 20 of 23 valid runs (87%) against 14 of 24 (58%) for Option A, and its interval clears A's. Option C's 3 of 4 rests on too few runs to say anything. Head to head, B was preferred in 12 of 19 pairings with A, and B's pass rate rose round by round while A's stayed near half.

items.text: The harbour sits under a violet sky; two moored boats, lights just coming on.
The fishing boat 'Marigold' returns at dusk.

blocks.title: How a run is scored
blocks.source:
flowchart LR
  R[Run] --> C{Required checks}
  C -- all hold --> J{Judge}
  C -- any fails --> F[Failed]
  J -- pass --> P[Passed]
  J -- fail --> F
  R -. no result .-> I[Invalid: excluded]

sections.reading: The excerpts show the difference the judge scored: Option B describes what is in the photo, Option A invents a boat name. The diagram shows how any run becomes passed, failed or invalid.
